The resolution aims to encourage the development of what the European Parliament calls in its technocratic jargon "the green infrastructure", it is necessary to understand the ecologization of urban spaces.This development is deemed, at the right term, necessary for a whole series of reasons such as public health, biodiversity, the quality of the water bodies and even the social.But as always, the springs of the ecological policy of the European Parliament are deprived.The first lever mentioned is to strengthen private sector investments.Never actually coercive proposals are envisaged to set up ecological planning at European level.Planning is left to private, for the best of their profits.This resolution is therefore not fully part of the fight against climate change.The global ecological crisis is that of the capitalist mode of production, encouraged by public policies currently implemented, in particular those of the European Union.I vote against.Quickly, ecological planning, stop the anti-ecological policies of the European Union.

Daniel Buda, in writing.- The report on the coherence of policies in favor of development has both the purpose of evaluating the progress reported by the commission and to identify the areas of improving the existing mechanisms of EU policy coherence.Even though the Union's political commitment has always been manifested, there are still difficulties in implementing this commitment through concrete measures.The coherence of policies in favor of development is a fundamental element for the implementation of the new agenda for sustainable development, but also in areas such as trade and finance, food security, climate change, migration and security.However, it is necessary to focus attention on the foreign policy of the Union given the context of the refugee crisis and the absence of stability in the vicinity of the Union.Therefore, the coherence of policies in favor of development must be found in the external actions of the Union in order to stabilize the EU neighborhood and to develop the best solutions in response to external challenges, which is why I expressed myself in favor of this report.

David Casa ,  in writing. ‒ Following tough discussions at EU committee level a compromise text has been presented underscoring the need for the strategy to focus on the sustainable management of forests and their multifunctional role from an economic, social and environmental point of view. It strongly rejects direct EU competence for forestry, but calls for coherence between the roles of the EU and the Member States in forestry-related policies. It acknowledges that the EU has a role to play in strengthening cooperation to tackle transnational challenges such as fires, climate change, natural disasters or invasive alien species. Finally, the report states that the implementation of the measures contained in forest management plans at the forest holding level must remain subject to national regulations and that bureaucratic burdens for EU forest owners are rejected. I can fully concur with this report and voted in favour.

Mr President, Mr Barroso, the Ceuta affair has come and gone, the Melilla affair has come and gone and now it is the suburbs that are on fire. The worldwide media is asking questions and, as for us, what are we doing? Drafting a legislative programme. To deal with what? Global warming, for example, which seems logical; when cars and schools are on fire, there is indeed a problem in terms of global warming and, therefore, in terms of respecting the Kyoto protocol. Alongside Mrs Fischer-Boel, we could, moreover, do slightly more to destroy our agriculture, such as it is; Mr Mandelson would obtain an agreement in Hong Kong and, for our part, we would have slightly higher levels of unemployment. Let us adopt a few more directives, and the mountain of legislation will end up rendering us quite powerless. I would even go so far as to propose a title for Mr Barroso’s legislative programme: ‘Operation smoke and mirrors’, for the programme is a smoke screen, concealing nice ideas, but ones that only mask tragedies. One final word, Mr Barroso: one Christmas day in the fifth century A.D., the Rhine froze over following a climate change. Thousands of chariots of fire crossed the Rhine, and Rome was plundered. Do you know what the Roman Senate was doing during that winter of 483? It was drafting a legislative programme. .

This text subject to the vote of the European Parliament aims to fix the budgetary framework for the European neighborhood policy, set up from 2004 and which today extends to 16 states located at the eastern and southern borders of theEU.Theoretically according to article 8 of the treaties, it is a question for the EU of developing with its neighbors closest to the so -called privileged relationships with a view to establishing "a space of prosperity and good neighborhood based on democracy andthe rule of law but also the market economy ".To implement it, the EU has a financial instrument for the PEV for the period 2014-2020, with more than 18 billion euros from which Russia will also benefit.If the instrument apparently contains positive elements, such as the fight against climate change or the promotion of decent work, it can be adapted on a case -by -case basis with increased help for "good students" and we know what are theCriteria that prevails for the EU: the liberalism and the readmission of immigrants come to the top of the criteria.So I have without state of mind voted against this report.

I am in favor of granting the 2012 landfill at the Institute for Gender Equality since, following the analysis carried out by the Court of Auditors, a more than good financial management from the Institute emerges.However, I consider it necessary to invite the Institute to update its guidelines on hiring to remedy the shortcomings found by the Court of Auditors and to identify satisfactory solutions for the problems that emerged in this regard.Overall, I consider myself satisfied with the management of the institute and for this reason I voted in favor.Plaudo to the progress recorded by the Institute as regards the completion of the staff of the staff, an aspect that contributes to its effective functioning, also demonstrated by the fact that in 2012, among other things, the Institute has developed two reports for presidenciesOn the themes "gender equality - climate change" and "violence against women - support for victims", completed the processing of the gender equality index, has started seven studies and developed an online database on resources oftraining regarding gender issues.

Madam President, I had originally hoped to speak on the Correia de Campos report but I can leave that, in order to save time for everyone else, and move on to the Arsenis report. First of all, thank you very much for calling me to speak about this report. Whatever one’s view on climate change and the destruction of our environment, or the problems with our environment, it is quite clear that it is important to monitor the use of some of the gases that could damage the environment. At the same time, I would ask our colleagues to be very careful and make sure that we do not use the green agenda as a form of protectionism. We quite often hear complaints from farmers in developing countries who say that we are introducing new standards – for example, sanitary and phytosanitary standards – in order to raise the bar for their exports to the EU, when what we could be doing is helping them to create wealth in their local communities by exporting food and other products to us. We complain about the way in which they use their land, even though it is not particularly damaging to the environment. That would be my first warning, but in general I would say that, whatever our views on climate change and the green agenda, it is important that we find consensus in these areas so that we can get the broadest possible support from as many people as possible.

Mr President, we in UKIP object both to the EU strategy on heating and cooling and the Commission’s new energy market design. It is clear that the EU strategy on heating and cooling would be used to reinforce the disruptive EU energy and climate policy that has already brought irreparable damages to the European industry and economy. With regard to the new energy market design, we opposed the implementation of the Third Energy Package in all Member States. The disaster of the EU over-commitment to unreliable, intermittent and hugely expensive renewables has now made clear that the EU climate policies have done far more economic damage than anything that could be envisaged as a result of climate change. They have forced up prices, undermined competitiveness and driven energy-intensive industries out of the EU altogether, taking their jobs and investment with them. The UK as an independent country will soon be free to choose how to make its own energy policy and to exploit and invest in lower-cost, reliable energy sources like coal, gas and nuclear.

Mr. President!First of all, a big thank you to my Swedish colleague Jessica Polfjärd.It has been a lot of fun to work together.It has been ambitious and it has become a good result, but given that I really wonder, how come the Moderates at home in Sweden are not ambitious in the climate issue and climate change?The evaluation made by the Climate Policy Council today in the morning was not just a saw - it was a chainsaw massacre of the current moderately -led government's climate work at home in Sweden.When it comes to the chairmanship of the Council of Ministers, it has been anything but ambitious when it comes to climate change.As soon as the word forest comes in, you have even acted rather as a brake pad in climate change.But you, Jessica, have done a great job.I hope you can be an inspiration for other moderates at home in Sweden.If nothing else, you may well call home to the prime minister and say that it is time to raise the ambitions even at home.Because it really is needed!

Mr. Chairman!Our debate is coming to an end and before the chairwoman sums up, I would like to say that the money and EU funds that we use or we can use are a very good thing.But I, who grew up in a dictatorship for an iron curtain, joined the European Union because I wanted to work, live, increase this space of freedom, democracy, and compliance with the law.I know that without this room we will not maintain or with climate change we will not fight, nor Ukraine will be useful and this space without observing the law has no value.So I can only express gratitude to all these colleagues who relentlessly fight for what is most important to all of us.Also express gratitude to the chairwoman of the European Commission, but with an appeal that we would not succumb to either national, party or any other tribal fights.The rule of law is the most important for all of us and concessions in this matter ...

Madam President, my dear colleagues, according to an IPCC report, 300 million people will be affected, within the next thirty years, by the rise of the seas, which is a consequence of global warming and the melting of ice.It is estimated that an increase of two meters from sea level is quite possible for the end of the century and that it will cause a considerable decline in the coastlines and will inevitably generate population movements.This climatic and ecological disaster augurs for future disasters in our landscapes and ecosystems, with potentially disastrous economic, human and social consequences.Obviously, it will lead to exiles and will serve as a pretext for mass immigration.I am of course particularly worried for the thousands of kilometers of coastline in metropolitan France and overseas which will undergo this maritime overflow and the worsening of floods, among other natural disasters.At best, it is necessary to put an end to this phenomenon.It is necessary, at worst, to anticipate it and prepare it.

Mr. President, the climate change observed pose a crucial problem to all the inhabitants of the planet.They must therefore be discussed in a responsible manner to anticipate and treat them.And to be effective, you should be aware of the entanglement of two phenomena.The first is only human responsibility, after 200 years of wild industrialization and productivity race, with a debauchery of uncontrolled carbon energy.The other is natural climatic cycles proven by the study of polar ice and caused, at the end of the last glaciation, an increase in temperature of more than 4 ° C and a rise of the seas of 120 meters.Man had nothing to do with it.So what to do?Cess to say that man and living organizations are responsible for everything;get out of the angelism of the Paris Agreement;Consider the phenomenal delay of the European Union in technological matters and innovative alternative solutions;stop establishing non-ecological free trade agreements;refuse the globalization and commodification of water, air, earth and anticipate their management;Limit pseudo-environmental constraints that lead the costs of cars, housing and food, and which justify more and more unbearable taxes for peoples.Let's go out in an emergency dogmatism and go to ...

Branislav Škripek, in writing.- Cohesion policy rarely focuses on mountain regions in the EU.Therefore, I welcome the call to create an EU program for mountain regions, which can be used for the basis of the already existing EU policies related to mountain regions only indirectly.E.g.Horizon 2020, Cosme, Life, Natura 2000, EU broadband strategy, EU strategy to adapt climate change and the like.However, I stayed in the final vote because I would welcome the current initiatives of the Carpathians no longer included in the EU strategy for the Danube region, but would be in a separate, separate EU strategy for the Carpathians.

Energy efficiency is a key element of the flagship initiative ‘A resource-efficient Europe’, which was announced within the framework of the Europe 2020 strategy. As the Commission’s communication ‘Road map for moving to a competitive low carbon economy by 2050’ shows, energy efficiency is one of the aspects of a low carbon economy that can help create new jobs in the short and medium term, through more intensive training, through further education and through programmes for better acceptance of new technologies, as well as through R&D and entrepreneurship. This proposed directive emphasises that the switch to a more energy-efficient economy will also improve the competitiveness of industry in the Union, thereby promoting economic growth and creating high-quality jobs in a number of sectors related to energy efficiency. That is obviously to be welcomed. Nonetheless, the fundamental question arises here as to whether global warming can actually be mitigated or limited by the planned measures. In view of the fact that this is primarily a natural phenomenon, it must be assumed that the proposed measures will mean substantial additional costs for public budgets and for companies which, in the end, will have no effect. All this at a time of crisis. I therefore voted against the proposed directive.

The interim report of the Temporary Committee on Climate Change does not contain any new ideas, thoughts or recommendations useful to the peoples of Europe regarding environmental protection. It perpetuates the EU’s well-known anti-popular policy of providing a ‘green’ excuse for the over-accumulation of capital. It confines itself to reproducing the findings of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change. The report considers the 2˚C ceiling on global warming to be a ‘strategic objective’ of the EU, while accepting that ‘such a level of warming would already heavily impact on our society and individual lifestyles’. It says nothing about the responsibility capitalists have assumed in over-exploiting natural resources. Instead of calling for measures at least to make monopolies more accountable, it fully adopts the multinational propaganda that we are all to blame for the aggravation of climatic conditions and stresses that ‘individual changes in lifestyle patterns are necessary’. The agreements reached in Kyoto, Bali, etc. have proved ineffective: their primary objective is not environmental protection, but the protection of capital and its profits. They commercialise the environment and develop a new, profitable economic sector: the green economy. The solution to environmental problems will not be provided by the multinationals and monopolies responsible for today’s situation, but by the peoples who have to suffer the consequences.

When reviewing the Copenhagen Summit and its results, one should employ common sense and look through the prism of the multitude of available environmental and economic data confirming that there is no such thing as global warming, and if it does exist, it is totally beyond human control, being caused purely by natural forces. By the way, we learnt last week that a significant portion of the environmental data used by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change was either knowingly falsified or misinterpreted. Seen in this light, it is good to see that the Copenhagen Summit has failed. I do hope that this failure will, first of all, bring a departure from the aggressive so-called ‘green’ politics. Secondly, politics will get back to genuine topics that really concern people in today’s economic recession. Thirdly, it will prevent the waste of taxpayers´ money on controversial green projects. Fourthly, it will create space for a matter-of-fact debate on the rational, efficient and cheaper provision of energy, and we will see the renaissance of nuclear energy. Ladies and gentlemen, when I meet my constituents, they shake their heads with incredulity over the topics we discuss here, failing as we do to deal with their real problems.

Brian Hayes ,  in writing. ‒ I voted to support this report as the PCA provides the basis for more effective engagement by the EU and its Member States with Vietnam. The agreement covers the EU’s standard political clauses on human rights, the International Criminal Court, weapons of mass destruction, small arms and lights weapons, and counter terrorism. Lastly the PCA strengthens the sectoral cooperation across a wide range of policy fields, such as taxation, migration, health, environment, climate change, energy, education and culture, labour, employment and social affairs, science and technology, and transport.

Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, I shall be abstaining from the vote on this motion for a resolution because I find it somewhat contradictory. It is, in fact, acknowledged within the resolution that economic cooperation between Russia and Europe has vastly improved over the last 10 years. It is recognised that Russia has strengthened relations in the areas of energy, trade, visa liberalisation, illegal immigration control, the fight against terrorism, climate change and foreign policy, and on issues such as Iranian nuclear weaponry, and peacemaking in the Caucasus and the Middle East. While we call for all these things, in the same resolution we strongly criticise Russia’s domestic situation. There is a general feeling of aversion towards and mistrust of Russia that does not represent a sound basis for the cooperation that we are calling for. This does not mean we should close our eyes to the democratic and human rights situation in that country, but I believe that support and trust are needed more than criticism at the moment, precisely in order to improve the human rights situation in Russia.

Mr President, the proposal for a Regulation on type-approval of motor vehicles and engines with respect to emissions from heavy-duty vehicles aims to establish a single set of principles for the construction of engines, thus ensuring a high level of protection for the natural environment. In fact, the proposed Union standards will also simply force small and medium-sized enterprises manufacturing engines out of the European market. In addition, the new engines are to run on alternative fuels, and manufacturers will be obliged to adjust accordingly all vehicles sold, registered or placed on the market. All the equipment used to measure emission of pollutants will also have to be adjusted. Only large transporters and corporations will be able to cope with research and organisational requirements of this magnitude. As regards new vehicles failing to comply with the provisions of this Regulation, national bodies will no longer accept certificates of compliance from 1 October 2014. As far as Poland is concerned, it is highly likely that many transport undertakings and engine manufacturing firms such as Andoria will simply cease to exist. The notion of Union legislation having the same effect in all Member States and serving all their interests is proving to be a myth. The elimination of weaker and poorer undertakings will obviously benefit large corporations, and these are mainly German. It is already apparent that most of the documents in the whole energy and climate change package may indeed ensure cohesion and economic development pursuant to the principles of sustainable development for large and wealthy countries and undertakings. Polish scientists estimate, however, that the package will cost at least PLN 500 billion. This will lead to economic collapse and to a huge increase in costs and food prices because of the need to replace transport vehicles. The population will be impoverished as a result.

Phil Wynn Owen is perceived, by the beautiful people of good European society, as a player involved in the fight against climate change.In 2012, he was also one of the members of the jury of a prize rewarding positive environmental initiatives: the "international Green Award".This award rewards large companies with a so -called "sustainable" development model each year.In 2011, for example, the UNIVERIGE anti-social multi-national multi-nationale won it.Unilever Ecolo: It is not the opinion of Elephant tea cooperators that she wants to die.In reality, Phil Wynn Owen, trained in Oxford, London Buisiness School and Harvard, alone embodies the illusion that there can be a "green capitalism".I think for my part that it is capitalism which is the cause of climate change, and that there can be no solution to this major problem of humanity by completely changing an economic model, but also social andpolicy.This is what I tried to demonstrate in my book: the green rule.Out of ecological planning and ecosocialism, no salvation for our planet and our ecosystem.

Mr President, up until recently, a swift and extensive enlargement of the European Union was suggested as a tremendous step forward, and as something meriting universal support. It was seen as a reunification of Europe and as the victory of the West in the Cold War. After the major enlargement of 2004, that climate changed dramatically. Public opinion in the old Member States does not experience this enlargement as a success, particularly as a result of the increasing exploitation of the disparity between high-wage and low-wage countries. The politicians too, are distancing themselves from it. This change is palpable in the report on the enlargement strategy that is the topic of today’s debate. Attention is being drawn to the EU’s absorption capacity, to the external borders, the costs that are involved in enlargement and to administrative problems that are attributed to the absence of a European constitution. As a result, Romania and Bulgaria are likely to be the last countries that are allowed to join in the short term. Other European states are being referred to the neighbourhood policy. Even for the three countries that have already been selected as candidate countries, no date of accession has been given. Everywhere across the western Balkans, in recognised states, as well as in federal states or protectorates striving towards independence, where groups of people who speak different languages and practise different religions, and who, in the 1990s, were at daggers drawn with each other, public opinion now expects miracles of a swift accession process to the European Union. The EU uses those expectations to demand reforms, and in that way, makes deep incursions into the administrative choices that are being made over there. The EU does not, for the time being, want enlargement, but it does want influence outside of its borders. That is why Bosnia and Herzegovina now have a tax system that nobody asked for, and the regional autonomy that was guaranteed in the Dayton agreement is being pushed back. According to the propaganda posters, it is thanks to the EU’s military presence that this country is on its way to joining the European Union. Public opinion in Montenegro and Kosovo, areas where four years ago, along with 12 Member States, the euro was introduced as legal tender, take it as read that they will soon be admitted to the EU as independent states, while the Hungarian-speaking people of Vojvodina expect protection against Slav dominance. So far, the EU’s actions have left all these people disappointed. Do we not have anything to offer those countries in the western Balkans other than the invitation to form a common market in the territory of the former Yugoslavia and to adapt their government and their economy to our wishes without them being able to join before 2020? My group can muster little enthusiasm for this proposal. We also recognise, however, that thanks to this text, it is possible to stress that the forthcoming referendum in Montenegro must be taken seriously and that the conflict about the use of the name Macedonia should be resolved quickly in sound consultation between Greece and its northern neighbour. What is also positive is that in Kosovo, a solution must be found in the short term which accommodates the needs of both the large Albanian majority and the Serbian and Roma minorities.

Mr President, a year ago I was at the Milan Climate Change Conference, and it must be said that a number of advances have been made since then. On that occasion we met representatives of the US delegation, as was also the case this time in Buenos Aires. Whereas in Milan the US representatives were still categorically denying the human contribution to climate change, this time their attitude had softened. They now had to acknowledge facts to the extent that they agreed to talk about the possible human contribution to climate change. Despite that admission, however, there is still a long way to go before we will persuade the United States of America to commit to a universal effort to prevent climate warming. There is thus a need for more common sense. We have numerous examples of how preventive action is far less costly than dealing with catastrophes after they have happened. That is why it is an economic absurdity that the United States is not rushing flat out to participate in cooperation on climate, instead of risking the entire planet trying to protect its competitiveness. Another step forward at Milan was Russia’s involvement, which enabled the Kyoto Protocol to come into force. That is an important factor as a political gesture, but whether it will be any more than that remains to be seen. I fear the worst: that climate targets under the current Kyoto agreement will barely make any further progress at all. Why should that be? At the conference the Minister of Housing, Spatial Planning and the Environment for the Netherlands, the country holding the presidency, said quite rightly that the problem for the future is, in particular, China’s emissions, whose rate of increase has come as a total surprise to the parties to the agreement. No disciplinary action can be taken under the Kyoto agreement, as China is not included among the industrialised countries that the emissions restrictions apply to in the first phase. Kyoto can do nothing, therefore, to bring two huge problems under control: the United States, which is at present responsible for a quarter of the world’s greenhouse gas emissions, and China, whose emissions are estimated to grow to four times those of the United States in ten years’ time. That means the world’s emissions will double within ten years. If that is the case, we will all perish. It is of the utmost urgency that we repair the situation now in order to strengthen climate policy, especially in China and India, to avoid making mistakes that cannot be put right later on while we await the second phase. Some of the taboos associated with Kyoto have to be removed, and it needs to be said that in some respects it is an unsuccessful way of solving the problem of climate warming. It would seem that, as a result of the targets for reductions in individual countries, the countries that are parties to the agreement are locked in a continuing struggle to protect their own interests. For that reason, we need a binding international ‘carbon dynamics’ approach, from which nobody can be excluded. In the globalising market economy, that is the only way to prevent international capital from transferring its production to places where emission limits do not exceed environmental norms. Consequently, we must set figures for emissions per tonne of production to act as emissions criteria for industry, and a careful definition of the theoretical minimum for emissions is needed for different sectors. We urgently need to think about energy in an entirely new way, structured above all around saving energy, increasing efficiency, and renewable and non-polluting forms of energy. Finally, I would like to express my profound gratitude to Commissioner Dimas, who took excellent account of the views of the Members of the European Parliament throughout the entire conference.

Brando Benifei, in writing.-Today I voted in favor of the Gabriel report on the EU-Isle Solomon agreement on the exemption from the visa for short-term stays.The text establishes an exemption for the citizens of the Union and for the citizens of the Solomon Islands that go to the other contracting part for a maximum period of 90 days on a period of 180 days.The exemption from the visa concerns all categories of people regardless of the reason for the stay as long as this is not linked to the performance of a paid activity.The exemption agreement from the visa constitutes a further demonstration of Europe's commitment to this region, an action focused on the promotion of democracy, human rights and a strengthened political dialogue.The approved text will certainly strengthen future relationships on issues such as environmental protection, especially in relation to climate change that threaten to cause significant damage in the archipelago.

I am voting for this motion for a resolution, the main objective of which is to reconcile the World Bank’s investments relating to energy with the development goals. I agree that energy strategy should tackle and facilitate the transition to environmentally sustainable energy development, and that the World Bank should adopt an approach to private sector development that provides the greatest benefit to the poor whilst simultaneously combating climate change. I find it regrettable that lending for fossil fuels continues to play a dominant role, despite the strategic objective being gradually to abolish financing for this type of project. I also note with concern that there is still little oversight of the majority of multilateral financing that is awarded through financial intermediaries: these should be pursuing clear development objectives. I call on the World Bank to reorient its current strategy from a large-scale, export-oriented energy model to small-scale, decentralised energy projects that respond more clearly to basic needs in rural areas. Finally, I would express my total agreement with the need for the World Bank clearly to identify and publicly disclose the development benefits before financing is committed.

Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, the European Union benefits from immense natural resources in terms of woodland, tree species, land and sea animals, nurtured by a wide range of climate conditions and obstructed by forms of behaviour that are not always proper. Fortunately, certain limits were established some time ago and the factors that hinder the conservation of this enormous wealth have been reduced. It is nevertheless worth considering that biodiversity constitutes an ideal mutual control mechanism between the animal, plant and mineral components of nature. It allows the conservation of the balances that facilitate dietary variety, prevent certain natural catastrophes, and help in the struggle against climate change and the greenhouse effect. I am in favour of approving this report because it is a first step away from declarations of principle, which are naturally nearly unanimously supported, towards concrete actions to safeguard biodiversity.

I welcome the historic agreement reached on MFF of EUR 1.8 trillion. More, the increases secured by Parliament for the key EU programmes in areas including health, research, mainstreaming gender and young people represent a big success of the negotiations held since 2018. The total amount of these top-ups is EUR 15 billion, and another EUR 1 billion will be put aside if unexpected future crises need to be addressed. The pandemic has given us new responsibilities and duties: the responsibility to make choices and the duty to do so in the interests of our European citizens. If we make a summary, it becomes obvious where we should invest: in the green economy, fighting against adverse effects of climate change, restore biodiversity, health, education, and in digital, democratic and social rights. We have managed to secure financing for the Green Deal and for a just transition and to stand up for a budget that is now greener, fairer and more socially just. We have to stay united, working hard for the well-being of the European citizens.

Mr. Chairman!The EU climate policy has been emphasized in public debate many times in public debate.The altar of the imaginary ideology of global warming consists of real interests of entrepreneurs, including Polish entrepreneurs.The Polish delegation with the new prime minister will participate in the summit.I am calling the Polish government to veto the findings of this peak!Instead of increasing the costs of energy, the Polish entrepreneur needs low taxes, limited administration and simple business rules.For Poland, the adoption of new proposals of the European Commission or even continuing the existing EU climate policy means an economic disaster.If the price of megawatt hours in Poland is about PLN 160, it will be PLN 320 in the near future.Expenses on the current of the average Polish family will increase many times.I call again to veto the findings of this peak!

As we heard in many previous speeches, carbon dioxide is an important and perhaps a key player in so-called ecological price determination, and is presented as the cause of climate change. I want to draw your attention to the fact that, according to scientific research, carbon dioxide in the atmosphere increases not before the earth heats up but only after it heats up. This warming process correlates with the sun’s activity so that warming is an effect rather than a cause. As a result, the main emitters of carbon dioxide after warming are the oceans. Of course, I am not against a reduction in carbon dioxide emissions caused by human activity but I think that we have to accept our responsibility for pollution that has health-related and other consequences, rather than responsibility for climate change. We should call a spade a spade.

Mr. President on this seventy anniversary of the Foundation of the Union - of our project -, Europe faces the most difficult situation since 1950. The Coronavirus pandemic is only the last challenge of a long list we have been facingIn the last ten years.From climate change to the new geopolitics, through digitalization, Brexit and Trump's choice in the presidency of the United States.It is true that Schuman said in his statement - and he has remembered a lot - that Europe would not be done at once, but through the creation of de facto solidarity.But he also said - and must be said at the same time - that the mint was the first step for a European Federation.Thus collected the spirit of the manifesto of Ventotene, a historical mission that we must culminate.Therefore, this moment is not the occasion of the small steps, but that of a big step forward.It is time to respond to the triple public, economic and institutional health crises with three unions: health, financial and politics.

Mr President, as a long-time member of Amnesty International I have to come to the conclusion that this Parliament can be the most effective advocate of human rights in the world. The Annual Report shows us that globalisation does not only send goods and money and investments around the world, but also values and good ideas. Today there are more democracies in the world than ever before. By the way, I do not know of any democracy which does not have a market-driven economic system implemented, and more countries than ever have abolished the death penalty. However, let me be quite frank here today. In the course of the discussions with members of other political groups, I have come to the conclusion that some of them misuse human rights to ride their ideological hobby horses. What do the Raif Badawis in the prisons of the world think when they hear that this report elaborates on financial transactions and labour standards? What do they think when they hear that there are demands of social dialogues and labour standards, medical policies and climate change? Of course, in the end, all committees of this House have dealt and deal with issues which have something to do with humans. But if the Subcommittee on Human Rights keeps on ever expanding the definition of human rights, then we might as well close down all other committees of this House. More importantly, we divide and divert the attention given to those who really need our engagement for human rights. Therefore, in order to send a signal, the ECR political group will this time abstain. )

Dear President, dear colleagues, the package, celebrated here as a big throw, passes the matter.A phantom fights.The man -made climate change is not secured knowledge, but a scientific hypothesis.There is a lot to say that he is an invention of lobby interests and researchers interested in research.My party therefore rejects all projects that aim to reduce so -called climate gas.We do not need an energy transition, no green energy, but rather a rational energy policy that is geared towards consumers and is founded in the market economy.Anyone who talks about a market design, whoever believes to know the best energies of tomorrow and for tomorrow, is subject to a blatant error.We cannot allow ourselves that as legislators.An demonstration is shown before the future and the individual rationality of the employees.If we do not measure ourselves to have a knowledge that raises us about it.Therefore, we should mottle these projects immediately.The commission's winter package belongs to ice.Immediately.

In order to tackle the current economic and financial crisis it is essential to promote inclusive, sustainable European growth, aligning the European Union’s budget with its main objectives. This report identifies a number of guidelines that will help to: promote employment; improve public expenditure on innovation, research and development; meet our climate change and energy objectives; improve education levels; and promote social integration. The European Semester, a new mechanism to strengthen European economic governance, should provide the chance to determine the best way to achieve these goals. It is essential to guarantee a certain level of coherence between the attainment of the results in question and the resources assigned to them at EU and national level, thereby improving synergies between European and domestic public investments. The European budget represents real added value, thanks to its ability to function as a catalyst to boost investment, growth and employment. The appropriations already planned must be kept at a suitable and flexible level of expenditure. Otherwise, their reduction would lead to the failure of the Europe 2020 Strategy. We call on the Commission to develop ambitious proposals for the provision of new own resources, based on a comprehensive impact assessment, in order to bolster competitiveness and economic growth.

Igor Soltes, in writing.- Changes in agricultural practice are structural or related to production processes.They make the agricultural sector one of the most dynamic sectors.As this sector is among the first to introduce new technology, the economy in the countryside can be successful and follow general economic development.The United Nations Organization for Food and Agriculture estimates that, due to the expected increase in the world population, it will be necessary to increase food supply.Thus, it is necessary to increase and improve agricultural production with fewer sources, especially due to pressure on natural resources and related effects on biodiversity, environmental vulnerability, climate change and land deficiency.However, I think the report is somewhat ambiguous and could be understood as if it supports innovations that are contrary to my principles.Although I understand that they are needed for progress, it must be ensured that they are friendly to health, the environment and do not produce negative consequences in other areas.I oppose the mention of drone and certain sections of the report giving the opportunity to support genetically modified mechanisms.Although the report advocates the idea that greater transparency in the supply chain and production can help consumers make more aware decisions in the purchase of products, with which I otherwise agree, I think that the report should be improved.Because of the aforementioned, I voted against.

Mr. President, in this global and interdependent world, there is no lack of challenges or conflicts.The European Union, therefore, needs a more coherent and more effective external action, which also demands a single voice and a single direction.And I think, Mrs. Mogherini, that her triple responsibility can facilitate that work.The European Union cannot locate itself.Together with our international partners we need, within the framework of the United Nations, maintain an international order that generates peace and stability and that is respectful of international law.In addition, there are global challenges that require global responses.I refer to climate change and also terrorism, of sad news in these days.The European Union must occupy a place of leadership in these global responses to these challenges, also global.I suppose, Mrs. High Representative, that these basic ideas will be present in the exercise of strategic reflection that the European External Action Service is carrying out.It seems to me that neighborhood policy must occupy a privileged place in that exercise.We cannot cover everything.Our neighborhood must be priority, in which challenges and conflicts proliferate in their southern and also oriental dimensions.I think of Libya, the results - general, disappointing - of the so -called "Arab spring" and the serious crisis in Ukraine for Russian intervention.I would like to underline a last aspect, as other speakers have already done: the need to continue deepening in the fields of security and defense.Certainly, at the moment, the economic crisis and the necessary fiscal consolidation do not allow large expenses in defense.But today's challenges and changes in the United States strategy demand that Europeans have a better and greater cooperation in the field of defense, since with the soft power, it certainly does not arrive.It is not enough.

Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, after this latest European Council we can fairly say that this is the Europe that we like: the Europe of choices, the Europe of farsightedness, the Europe that takes care of its interests and projects its role onto the world. This was a much-needed, albeit unexpected final spurt, but a really welcome one. It is not the first time that we have been on the point of rolling back down but have made it up the slope again by giving it our best effort: we did so with the customs union, the single market and the euro. Today we are doing it with energy and the fight against climate change. We must not stop now: that would be an unforgivable own-goal. The Commission must do its part by translating the Council's decisions into legislative proposals on which Parliament can work in depth. The Council should assess national plans on a majority basis. Above all, we must not stop on the road to a political Europe. As the President of the Italian Republic, Giorgio Napolitano, said in this Chamber during the last part-session, the Constitution is not a caprice, a whim or mere ornament. Without new rules, a legal personality, a political and social soul and the Charter of Rights, Europe is in danger of declining again. That is why we anxiously await the declaration of 25 March. Mrs Merkel said yesterday that the declaration will not talk about God, and that is all right, because God holds anyone who is sincerely Catholic and Christian in His heart. However, the declaration must not fail to talk about the Constitution. After last week’s successes, it would be disappointing if we came up with a vague declaration that did not talk about Europe's successes or mention the great advances of the last 50 years or, most of all, did not sketch out this great goal of the European Constitution.

Mr President, the fight against global warming has, without doubt, become one of the European Union’s most important objectives. A significant factor in this is, I think, a rational policy for reducing emissions of carbon dioxide and greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. In Parliament’s motion for a resolution, which has been drafted before the Cancún conference, there is a part which mentions a significant reduction – by more than 20% – in CO2 emissions from Member States. It seems that, in proposing a policy of this kind, the Union is not looking at the serious consequences for the economies of its Member States. While there is such a large reduction on the part of the Union, there is a very feeble statement of the Union’s position in relation to a reduction in gas emissions in the United States or the countries of Asia. This is a great mistake. Today, when Europe is experiencing economic decline, we should concentrate more on measures intended to strengthen the Union’s economy, and not burden it with additional costs. It is not the Member States of the European Union which are the major emitters, but the rapidly growing economies of developing countries such as China and India, and they do not intend to reduce emissions. Industrial production, and in consequence jobs, might, therefore, be exported to countries outside the European Union. Our economy will become weaker, and emissions will not fall, but rise. This policy is going nowhere. Therefore, this type of policy direction in the field of fighting global warming should be reconsidered.

Mr. President, Mrs. Georgieva, of course thank you very much and all my congratulations, also to the speakers and the entire team of the Committee.It is of course an elaborate budget, worked with effort, with sweat - let's say - and with an indisputable result.But let me tell immediately that the rule of the two years referred to by Mr. Arthuitof this Parliament and distant, above all, of the convenience or need of the European Union as a whole.It can be said that politics is the art of getting the possible.OK.And surely we have the maximum possible, in the sense that the limit of this "possible" is marked by the Council, and marks it clearly and forcefully - "Available Resources", as Mrs. Georgieva said.They do not ask us as Parliament that we accept this logic, because if this Parliament accepts this logic, it is accepting to simply be resonance chamber of decisions that are already taken in advance.The problem is not for this Parliament or for my group;It is for the European Union, for the commitments that we have taken as a European Union in relation to climate change, the Europe 2020 strategy, the sustainable development objectives.All these commitments are not respecting this budget.The 200 million appeared in the last minute mean what they mean for the respective games - for horizon 2020, for Cosme, for the mechanism "connect Europe", for Erasmus.You speak, as I have done this morning, with Mr. Bourguignon, of the European Research Council, and you will see what it means in real result, in real budget value.The same happens with the 500 million of the youth employment initiative that will appear - we say - throughout the year, far, far from the minimum continuity that would mark 6 billion for four years or 1,500 for each of them.And if we add the question of the Code of Conduct, which Mr. Tarand reminded us, the conclusion is clear: we are also losing the battle of credibility, the battle of the image and respect.When we protect debatable actions of ex -women of the Commission, we are harming in the same proportion our own institutional credibility.Last But Not Least, we have a budget, but we don't have MFP.We will discuss it in a few minutes.Our group has shared the effort and has accompanied them here.We cannot accompany you, of course, in the final vote.

Monika Flašíková Beňová, in writing - the interest of the European Union should be to maintain constructive relations in the long term, which aims to face common global challenges, such as combating terrorism, organized crime, but also challenges in the field of climate change or development of new technologies.Unfortunately, the Russian Federation has been actively using a hybrid war in recent months, wiping in deliberately between military/paramilitary activities and political activities.Moreover, against the spirit of good neighborly relations and contrary to international law, rules and standards, it has undertaken intentional events aimed at destabilizing neighboring countries.The EU is interested in improving relations with the Russian Federation, but it is its duty to use all the means to prevent such proceedings by the Russian Federation.

Mrs. Chairman!We write history with the European Climate Act.We state that climate change is a cross -border problem that requires cross -border solutions.No European country can sit back with his arms crossed and expect others to take the tow.Everyone must contribute to the EU becoming climate -neutral by 2050.Therefore, we are now creating an independent European climate council, which will sit in Copenhagen as part of the European Environment Agency.The Climate Council must guide us when we make legislation and ensure that our climate measures follow both the Climate Act and the Paris Agreement.To achieve the goal of climate neutrality in 2050, we have set up a 2030-part goal.We must have reduced our CO2 by at least 55 percent by 2030. I had wanted a significantly higher reduction target.We Social Democrats went to the negotiations with a desire to get a sub -target of at least 60 percent.But politics is also the possible art, and a few years ago a 40 percent target was what characterized the debate.So I feel like we don't want to stand in the corner with our arms crossed just because we didn't get everything exactly as we wanted.Today we take a big step forward for the climate and it is hammering necessary.That is why I support the Climate Act.

Countries that have long been minerals, such as the United States, Japan and European countries, have to face increasing competition for access to strategic minerals and supply security.This situation gives developing countries the possibility of taking advantage of their natural resources.If it is true that unprecedented global demand for minerals and other natural resources represents a unique opportunity to allow mining extraction to contribute to sustainable development, it also poses considerable challenges to developing countries.The exploitation of high -value natural resources such as petroleum, gas, ores and wood is an important source of conflicts around the world, in particular in a context of increasing competition for access to renewable resources increasingly andrarer like land and water.Environmental degradation, population growth and climate change are further aggravating this situation.The mismanagement of land and natural resources contributes to creating new conflicts and obstructs the peaceful resolution of current conflicts.

Sergio Gutiérrez Prieto, in writing.- The Paris Agreement is the first legally binding international agreement adopted in climate change.It was adopted in the 21st Cop of the CMNUCC, which took place in Paris from November 30 to December 12, 2015. I have voted in favor so that both the Union and the seven member states that have completed the ratification process, canDeposit its ratification instruments at the UN Headquarters in New York on Friday, October 7, allowing Paris Agreement to enter into time for COP22, which will take place in Marrakech from November 7 to 18, 2016.Socialists think that the Union cannot be left behind other world powers when it comes to ratifying, so they have favorably voted the resolution that enables the Council to formally adopt the ratification decision by urgent written procedure.

Mr. President, Lord Commissioner, the drought in the European Union affects more than one third of the continent and today the scenario is dramatic.For example in Portugal, according to the Portuguese Institute of Sea and atmosphere, 66% of the territory is in extreme drought and 33% in severe drought.You must do more.It is necessary to bet on: monitoring and prevention strategies, with the support of entities such as the European Drought Observatory;Territory evaluation plans, which should identify the most vulnerable groups to these extreme climate phenomena and include adaptive adaptation measures;and also measures to mitigate the risk of drought and heat vacancies.Unfortunately it is no longer enough to try to reverse the impact of climate change.We will have to learn to live with them, but continue to work to mitigate them and thus ensure the health of our planet and those who live in it.

This report endorses the second revision of the Cotonou agreement while issuing reserves.This position challenges all logical: if there is reservations, why approve the agreement?For my part, I oppose this new version of the Cotonou agreement.It does not change the free swinger logic that underlies it, for the benefit of multinationals and to the detriment of the peoples of the States of Africa, the Caribbean and the so-called "ACP" Pacific.The economic partnership agreements are not called into question, the control of so -called "illegal" migrants is reinforced, as for the additions so much about the fight against climate change, they are concretely the sole participation of the ACP statesAt the carbon market, which demonstrated its ineffective and dangerousness.I vote against this text and denounce it.

Madam President, I think many people will be watching the news about COP28 and wondering what’s the actual point of it, not just because of where it is, but because year on year we fail to act. Of course there needs to be a dedicated space for multilateralism, but COP isn’t working, and one of the key reasons for that is that the Global North has failed in its responsibility towards those areas of the world that are most affected by climate change. We promised 100 billion by 2020, even though they needed actually 4 trillion, but we couldn’t even deliver on that. And even of the monies that were delivered upon, 71% of that public climate finance was in the form of loans. Now let’s think about what that actually means. Last year, Pakistan was at the front line in terms of the climate crisis, with floods displacing 33 million people. So when they should have been spending money rebuilding homes in the aftermath, they were using 50% of the country’s annual revenue to pay back foreign creditors. If this is the way forward, we’re doing the world a disservice and we and they cannot afford it.

Lara Comi, in writing.- I expressed my vote in favor of the partnership agreement with the Republic of the Philippines, which would bring great advantages for the Filipino State in terms of economic development, financial support, reduction of poverty, social inclusion, respect for human rights, promotion of thenational peace and security.In addition, cooperation with the European Union would include assistance measures to the Republic of the Philippines in the effective preparation for natural catastrophes and to facilitate the implementation of policies to face climate change.

Mrs. President, I have voted in favor of this report so that Parliament is firm demanding legal obligations for the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.However, the position of the European Union is not exempt from paradoxes.How to think that the market, and especially the financial market, can be the way to a sustainable society?How to imagine that the same instrument that encourages infinite consumption and irresponsible investment can replace the State in the ecological transition?I cannot deny that I have doubts about the capacity of the European Union to implement the recommendations of this report against the interests of the wildest capitalism.I hope this report does not stay alone in words.Other policies yes, but also another economic model, another way of life.Otherwise, the fight against climate change is lost in advance.

The foundation of the EU’s promotion policy has to be better defined. Awareness of the opportunities inherent in local production and short food supply chains must be raised by implementing promotional measures. Developing short food supply chains and local markets can create jobs at local level, and local farming systems will restore added value for farmers. European farmers and producers are facing new challenges and have to apply production systems that adapt to these challenges, such as climate change, lower soil fertility and biodiversity. Promotion activities have to focus more on quality and on products produced at local level. Consumers within the EU are increasingly interested in the tastes of quality products as well as those that have come about through tradition. This is why I support the move to draw attention to a diverse programme of the tastes of Europe that meets consumers’ tastes too, within the framework of promotion measures. I also believe it is important for the individual promotion and information activities to bring citizens and producers together. As part of school programmes providing fruit and milk for pupils, for example, children can be brought closer to the work of agricultural producers. By visiting farms and facilities they can gain first-hand experience of the food production process and how the common agricultural policy works.

Mr President, the earlier references to the so-called evidence about Himalayan glaciers need to be elaborated on. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change said in 2007 that they would disappear by the year 2035. The Sunday Times has recently discovered that the report was ultimately based on an interview given to the New Scientist by an Indian scientist, Mr Hasnain in 1999. Mr Hasnain has subsequently said that this was based on personal estimates and did not mention the year and did not carry out any formal research. If our conclusions on the hypothesis of climate change are to be based on evidence, then that evidence must be irreproachable. It must not be manufactured and it must not be invented.

Mr. President, this resolution draws up the difficult portrait of Burkina Faso today.Allow me, however, a reminder: the dialogue is and remains a pillar in Burkina.Between populations, ethnicities, religions, national cohesion still exists.In reality, we are here faced with a political and territory crisis.These crises are combined with the consequences of global warming.Burkina Faso is fighting so that extreme poverty is not the fertile soil of jihadism.Our countries and Europe have a major responsibility and our action is misunderstood by the population.We come out of a G5 again which is a failure.An addition of weaknesses will never make a strength, and it is urgent for France, Europe and the rest of the international community to rethink the Sahelian strategy.It is time to take a sincere and frank assessment and learn from our long history of failures.It is with the populations that it is necessary to rebuild stability.

Mr.President!Mrs. Commissioner!Mr.Commissioner!Dear colleagues!This report comes at a very important time when we have to choose the way forward for the EU's future and common climate and energy policy.The EU was brave in 2008 when we chose to take the lead in the fight against climate change.Our policy has also meant that we have created new green jobs in Europe.It is a policy that I think we should continue.Therefore, it is crucial that we continue the three binding goals for CO2 reductions, renewable energy and energy savings respectively.In the EU, we spend over 500 billion every year.euro on importing oil and gas.This is equivalent to more than Poland's total gross domestic product.It is money that could be used much better: In investments in Europe for renewable energy and energy savings.It will also create jobs and growth in the European countries - well to feel local workplaces that cannot just be moved to China and elsewhere.Not least, it will also mean cheaper energy in the long term.Binding and clear goals are also needed to attract investments to new technologies.Europe must create its own energy production itself, and investments in e.g.Sea wind turbines are crucial for us to get closer to self -sufficiency.Therefore, the Commission's play is not ambitious enough!There are lack of goals for energy savings and a larger proportion of renewable energy.It is crucial that Parliament shows the way forward.We must send a clear signal to the member states that one must continue along the ambitious path.It is the only way we can ensure Europe's independence of animals imported energy.Today, Putin determines our energy prices!It's not the renewable energy!It's Gasprom that decides!Therefore, I would strongly recommend that we vote for three binding goals tomorrow.

Madam President, the issue of climate—resilient fisheries and aquaculture is indeed very important. But we need to address the negative impacts of fisheries on climate change, and we can start to tackle the problem by fully implementing the common fisheries policy and the related legislation that we already have. But I wanted to focus on the fact that the sector itself has an important role to play and must contribute to global CO2 reduction efforts. A recent study published by the scientific journal Nature showed that industrial fishing – in particular, bottom trawling – generates more CO2 emissions than air travel. Why? Because when trawls are dragged along the sea floor, large amounts of carbon are released, which increases global warming and makes the sea more acidic. It also has an adverse effect on plankton and entire marine ecosystems, which produce more or less 80% of the oxygen on Earth. So, on World Oceans Day, let us take concrete steps to end bottom trawling by EU vessels worldwide. Without this ban, we cannot achieve climate neutrality, and this is the only option if we want to be coherent with the European Green Deal and the EU’s targets to reduce CO2 emissions.

The European Union has its own responsibilities in the impasses and blockages recorded in international negotiations.It claims leadership in the efforts to combat climate change but it itself persists in emission reduction goals below those recommended by the IPCC.But more than setting goals, a realistic definition of the means to achieve them is required.IRONIC AND SADLY IS THE DEPENSE ECONOMIC CRISIS IN WHICH WE ARE PLATED WHO MORE TO CONTAIN THE EMISSIONS OF GREEN EFFECT GAS.Centered on market instruments that have already shown their failure, ineffectiveness, their perversity, the European Union insists on refusing to face the need for diversification of the instruments used to achieve reduction goals.The climate, for many, is still a good pretext for profitable business opportunities than the reason for serious and genuine concern about the future of the planet we live in.It is important to mark the inconsistency of policies, for example, of liberalization and deregulation of international trade, which significantly increase greenhouse gas emissions inherent in the satisfaction of human needs.And, by the way, it is also important to remember the millions that, since 2009, with a large media, have announced for mitigation and adaptation to climate change.What is made of this money?What is made of the so -called quick starting financing and what should follow you?

Mrs. President, China's rise in the world is one of the most important events of the last thirty years.The world scenario has changed.Europeans have to maintain a constructive relationship with China, and that does not mean abdicating our values ​​or our interests, nor hiding our differences.China's collaboration is obviously very relevant to successfully face global challenges, for example, climate change.On this possibility of bilateral agreements to solve problems in Africa or in African countries, those triangular agreements that you mentioned, Mrs. Mogherini, I am a bit skeptical.But, in short, we are in a world in which economic and commercial relations have been globalized, and that economic openness and the impulse of trade have allowed the great economic and social development of China;But we are also a great export power, and many jobs in Europe - I always say - depend on our commercial penetration capacity, even in the Chinese space.That is why we should try to reach solutions in our commercial discrepancies, while avoiding dumpings.And I highlight - and end - the need to conclude the bilateral investment agreement.It seems essential to search for this balanced pitch for reciprocal investments, and I hope that the impulse given by the recent summit of July 16 allows a prompt conclusion.

Rapporteur Konrad Szymański wanted to disavow his own report by a postponement in committee but could not do so for procedural reasons.This text was indeed bad.The question of warming/climate change has occupied the front of the stage for many years to make Europeans feel guilty at the slightest opportunity.The reduction of greenhouse gas emissions is the battle horse of the well-righteous commission.The EU is only responsible for 11% of these emissions worldwide.Despite the economic common sense, before the increase in energy prices, the Commission only offers costly and random renewable energies, such as wind and a drop in GHG emission quotas for Member States, or aincitement to pollute elsewhere than in Europe.Insecurity remains as to the supply of renewable energies.These resources are not reliable enough or flexible to respond quickly to the rapid changes that take place in demand.European energy policy is not balanced and this is reflected in the irresponsible proposals of the Commission which only increase the normative shackles of the Union.

Mr President, the report we are debating today is a symbol of the arrogance and mainstream blindness of Parliament. It is dangerously close to suppressing freedom, democracy and solidarity with the weakest in society. In regard to freedom of thought, there is nothing worse than insisting that only one scientific opinion is correct and denouncing other ideas. In regard to democracy, there is nothing worse than giving political blessing to such an opinion and trying to control people’s lives accordingly. In regard to solidarity with the weakest, there is nothing worse than pouring foodstuffs into car petrol tanks and watching people die from hunger. Such policies will not save the planet. The only winners will be the producers of subsidised rapeseed and manufacturers of windmill components. Taking into account that the report attempts to suppress the exchange of opinions, dictates what the scientific results should be and overlooks the needs of the poorest in society, in no way can I give it my support. I think that the Temporary Committee on Climate Change should be immediately dissolved. In conclusion I just want to say that I come from the Czech Republic and I can proudly say that, unlike other politicians, President Václav Klaus’s thinking has not become warmer and his brain has not become green.

Mr President, I completely agree with Collega Sartori, president of the Commission for Industry, Research and Energy.The proposal to modify the ETS Directive, as formulated, gives paper white to the Commission to intervene on the auction mechanism, to manipulate the market of shares with the aim of checking, or even predetermining, the price of CO2.Furthermore, the proposal underestimates or completely neglects the impact on the manufacturing industry and in particular on the high -intensity sectors, such as the steel one, who are laboriously trying to return to the prescrrriori production levels.As has emerged from the conclusions of the last international conference on climate change, any binding commitment by other large countries global emitters, comparable with European ones, will be concretized perhaps not before 2020. Any intervention that involves a unilateral increaseThe European effort to reduce emissions already set to 2020 therefore appears completely unjustified and unacceptable.The European Union should go beyond the unilateral political and regulatory approach linked to climatic dumping, insisting with a policy of duties on the borders of the European Union.

Owing to the inclusion of several points that are extremely harmful to Polish sovereignty, the Solidarna Polska [United Poland] delegation within the Europe of Freedom and Democracy Group was unable to vote in favour of the motion for a resolution. I believe that nobody whose aim is for Poland to retain its sovereignty and to cooperate within the European Union on an equal footing can, in clear conscience, support measures that will lead to the creation of a single European superstate. Including through the introduction of a requirement to allocate as much as 20 % of expenditure to tackling climate change. The EU’s current policy in this area  will lead to a twofold rise in energy prices, a loss of competitiveness for Polish industry and the disappearance of several hundred thousand jobs, and may jeopardise Poland’s economic growth. There is a lack of any clear provisions concerning the reform of the common agricultural policy, in particular as regards ensuring equal conditions of competitiveness and equal payments for farmers in Poland and in other Member States or on the introduction of a new European tax to provide direct EU financing, without going through the Member States. The motion for a resolution merely calls for the introduction of a European Financial Transaction Tax. The introduction of an EU tax is a step towards the creation of an EU federal state.

I agree with the proposal of the Decision of the Council on the conclusion of the framework agreement on a comprehensive partnership and cooperation between the European Union and its Member States, on the one hand, and the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, on the other, Lochbihler MP.The European Union and the Socialist Republic of Vietnam have signed a number of agreements in the last 30 years to regulate their relationship.This agreement will be replaced by an existing legal framework that was regulated by the 1995 agreement between the EU and Vietnam and from 1980 on cooperation between the European Economic Community and the Member States of the Association of Southeast Asia.I believe that this agreement will contribute to the greater economic and political participation of the European Union in Southeast Asia.The agreement will increase cooperation with Vietnam on many political issues, such as taxation, migration, health, environment, climate change, energy, education and culture, work, employment and social policy, science and technology and traffic.I believe this is the next step in increasing the activity of the European Union in Southeast Asia and intensifying cooperation with ASEAN countries.

I voted for this report, which seeks to make EU humanitarian aid more effective. The European Consensus on humanitarian aid is major step forward. Nevertheless, the review of its action plan must be more coherent, using objectives that are more measurable and indicators that are more reliable. That is the only way that we will manage to deliver aid more effectively. Given the increasing number and severity of natural disasters caused by climate change, I agree with the position put forward that it is important, not just to provide one-off aid, but also to provide support for communities’ own disaster-preparedness capabilities: the Hyogo action plan needs to be strengthened. Efforts also need to be concentrated on human rights issues arising from internal conflicts and complex crises, improving the capacities of the bodies involved to access populations; this will only be possible by making a clear distinction between military, political and humanitarian roles. I also agree with the effective application of a European rapid-intervention capability.

Farmers play a key role in the green transition and the construction of a resilient agricultural sector.The adoption of sustainable agricultural practices, such as precision agriculture and biological agriculture, lead to the reduction of the use of chemicals on the grounds, safeguarding natural resources and attenuating the negative effects of climate change in order to protect our health and the healthBiodiversity.Although the transition to carbon -free agriculture is a European Union priority, it is essential to be aware of the specificities with which farmers are faced with different regions of the European Union, especially those of the ultra -peripheral regions.Struttered orography and soil type of these regions make it impossible to use heavy machinery and require arduous manual work, which puts them at a disadvantage against large surfaces.The way towards a sustainable and resilient agricultural sector cannot be reached only by farmers.EU policies should recognize and make available the tools needed to support agricultural workers, properly investing in research and necessary infrastructures, essential to facilitate the adoption of sustainable practices and ensuring a fair transition that leaves no one behind.

The Republic of Palau is a constructive partner of the EU in the context of the Cotonou Agreement. In this regard, the agreement on the waiver of short-stay visas represents a culmination of the deepening of relations between the European Union and the Republic of Palau. It is also a clear signal that the EU is seeking to facilitate political dialogue with Palau in terms of protecting the environment in relation to climate change, defending human rights, and gender equality. Last but not least, I supported EU-Palau agreement on the short-stay visa waiver because the country does not present any threat to the EU in terms of irregular migration and security issues.

Ruza Tomasic, written.- Although the European Union policies are largely aimed at preserving and protecting the environment, it can be observed that most of the focus is aimed at solving climate change problems, while a far less attention is given to air quality.Given that the poor air quality contributes to premature mortality, diseases, productivity loss, loss of crop yields and damage to buildings, it is clear that the emissions of atmospheric pollutants are a health and environmental problem.I support the fact that the report is recognized by the need to reduce the negative influences and risks that the contaminated air has on the environment and human health, but I believe that the establishment of new, elevated limitations will not achieve much, since individual Member States cannot achieve default goals.I believe that it is first and foremost necessary for each Member State to determine the goals that it will be able to really fulfill, and in accordance with this I voted restrained.

Mr. President, Mr. Commissioner, Madam Rapporteur, Dear colleagues, the subject of the impact of climate change on vulnerable populations is a much more complex subject than it seems.And yet, it is a major subject and stake, complex because the impact of climate change can take the habit of a so -called natural disaster - cyclone, mud flow or fire -, an event then undergone forwhich we will provide a humanitarian response of circumstance.But it can also take the insidious habit of a territory which gradually deserted or sea level which is gradually rising.The subject is also complex because when we talk about vulnerable populations, we immediately think of Africa, Asia, the small island states of the Pacific, but not necessarily in Latin America, the Arctic Populations or evento vulnerable populations of our own European territory.Still complex, because the link between climate change and cascade consequences such as famines, economic crises and conflicts is all the more difficult to make it stretch in time.However, experts agree to highlight a link between climate change and most of the great conflicts that shake the world today.Complete always, because from our European window, the slightest allusion to situations that can lead to population movements, even local, generate the fear of the migrant at the gates of Europe, which will of course arrive without a label "Be careful, Iam a climate move ”.In this context, there is an emergency at all stages of this process, which should concern 200 million individuals in 2050: urgency to reduce our emissions, an emergency to anticipate the consequences of climate change, to adapt the territories in particular, and urgencyAlso to recognize the status of displaced due to the climate and to advance on a common terminology on an international scale.The European Union has a responsibility and must act within the framework of the Green Pact for Europe and all its variations.I will of course vote, Madam Rapporteur, this report.

Madam President, I register for false compared to what has been said, because this ITER project is not relevant since it arrives too late.What does the IPCC say?He says that, to resolve the problem of global warming, you have to manage to produce electricity without CO2 before 2050. However, the ITER project has been very late and the first prototype to manufacture electricity will not happenBefore 2050.
